title: Examining the Quasi-Public Spaces in Commercial Complexes
central_proposition: Commercial complexes function as quasi-public spaces, and their physical features, accessibility, safety, and social activities promote sociability, psychological well-being, and consumption, thereby contributing to social sustainability.

concept_definitions.name: public
concept_definitions.definition: Refers to spaces with a strong relationship among community and state, belonging to a residence that is open and shared with the community as a whole, without discrimination.

concept_definitions.name: quasi-public spaces
concept_definitions.definition: Urban spaces, such as commercial complexes, that are controlled by private authorities but are easily accessible to all people, serving mixed public and private functions.

concept_definitions.name: social sustainability
concept_definitions.definition: A set of measures and policies aiming to improve quality of life and equal access to natural and artificial environments, focusing on assets like consumption, education, skills, income, employment, and gender equity, promoting eco-friendly behavior and connections between people and the bio-physical environment.

argument_structure: The paper reviews the evolution of public and quasi-public spaces, highlighting the emergence of commercial complexes as modern civic centers. It then empirically investigates the physical features of these complexes and their role in promoting sociability and social sustainability, using a questionnaire survey and observations to validate the proposed relationships.
mechanism_or_causal_logic: Commercial complexes, through their design and management, provide specific physical features (social activities, accessibility, physical aspects, safety, and circulation) that create a welcoming, secure, and stimulating environment. This environment facilitates social interaction, relaxation, entertainment, and a sense of community, which in turn promotes sociability, enhances psychological well-being, and increases consumption, ultimately contributing to social sustainability.

testable_hypotheses_or_predictions: Commercial complexes exhibit specific physical features (social activities, accessibility, physical aspects, safety, circulation) that define them as quasi-public spaces.
These identified physical characteristics positively influence sociability, social integration, and psychological well-being within commercial complexes.
bridge_warrants: The concept of quasi-public spaces bridges the traditional dichotomy of public and private spaces, integrating elements of both.
The study connects the physical environment of commercial complexes to psychological needs such as social interaction, enjoyment, and relaxation.
The findings link environmental design features to broader concepts of social sustainability, including tolerance, community, and public trust.
model_structure: The paper implicitly proposes a model where specific environmental factors (social activities, accessibility, physical aspects, safety, and circulation) within commercial complexes act as antecedents, leading to consequents such as increased sociability, enhanced psychological well-being, and higher consumption, ultimately contributing to social sustainability.
limitations: The study findings, based on data from three commercial complexes in Hangzhou City, China, may not be representative of China in general.
Further research in other cities is needed to study the validity and reliability of the identified factors of quasi-public spaces.

paper_metadata.title: Examining the Quasi-Public Spaces in Commercial Complexes
paper_metadata.crossref_title: Examining the Quasi-Public Spaces in Commercial Complexes
paper_metadata.crossref_abstract: Commercial complexes are steadily expanding in size and function and plying roles as quasi-public spaces. This study investigated quasi-public spaces in contemporary commercial complexes by posting two questions: the physical features of quasi-public spaces in commercial complexes and how these characteristics promote sociability in commercial complexes? To answers these questions, a questionnaire survey was administered, and various observations were made in Intime City, Wanda Plaza and Western City Square, three prominent commercial complexes in Hangzhou City (Zhejiang Province, China), to enrich the analysis. Confirmatory factor analyses were used to examine the collected data. The results show that commercial complexes are also used as quasi-public spaces: they provide a more secure and well-maintained environment, playful conversations take place freely and democratically, promote socialization, and also increase consumption. In the existing literature, there is a dearth of theoretical and empirical studies on the emergence of quasi-public spaces.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: The paper extends traditional Public Space Theory by examining how privately owned commercial complexes function as 'quasi-public spaces' and their implications for urban social life.

The paper applies Social Sustainability Theory to the context of commercial complexes, proposing how the design and management of these spaces can contribute to or detract from social sustainability outcomes.

mechanism_chain.description: The paper proposes a conceptual mechanism linking the characteristics of commercial complexes as quasi-public spaces to social sustainability.
